title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
summary: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer. On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place. Continue reading...

title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
summary: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. title: All Blacks have ‘no gas in the tank’ but stats show it’s England who should be out of juice
summary: Figures indicate England’s players have far more rugby miles in their legs than Saturday’s opponents but Borthwick has managed to balance heavy schedule The prevailing narrative emerging before England’s rematch with New Zealand on Saturday is that the All Blacks are running on fumes. The forwards coach, Jason Ryan, has said that “there is not much juice in the tank” while Graham Henry, who led them to the 2011 World Cup title, has continued the theme in even starker terms. “It’s the end of the season and we’re buggered. They’ve just got no gas in the tank.” It is understood that narrative has raised a number of eyebrows within the England camp. The view, as England seek to clinch a third straight win over New Zealand for the first time in the history of the fixture, is best summed up as, “welcome to our world”. We are nearing the end of a gruelling year for the All Blacks, who give the impression they cannot wait for their season to end, but the grind in England, that which led to Maro Itoje being ordered to take the summer off, is at the very least comparable. title: Chess: Magnus Carlsen comes to London as Gukesh and Sindarov battle in Geneva
summary: The world No 1 heads a record field of 800 competitors for the XTX Markets Super Rapid Magnus Carlsen’s forthcoming participation in the Super Rapid at the XTX Markets London Classic has triggered a flood of entries after the organisers announced that the event’s capacity at the London Novotel West in Hammersmith on 5-6 December would be increased from 500 to 800, making it the largest single tournament ever staged on English soil, though surpassed internationally by Germany’s Grenke Open at Karlsruhe. The world No 1, making a very rare appearance in an open tournament, is likely to be paired with an opponent rated in the low 1800s in the first round. title: No sanctions and no recrimination: Cricket Australia ball tampering forum to include 2017-18 Ashes series
summary: Scope of forum includes Australia’s entire 2017-18 season Independent process to be led by senior counsel Fiona McLeod The scope of a forum set up to provide Australian players and staff on the 2018 tour of South Africa with an opportunity to air their views on sandpapergate has been broadened to include experiences from the 2017-18 Ashes series. Cricket Australia (CA) on Friday revealed the terms under which those who want to can share their experiences in a “safe and confidential” environment, after the ball tampering saga blew up again following the publication of Usman Khawaja’s memoir earlier this month.
